subject: Marketplace private-offer MAP & procurement timeline — BlueSky Analytics
messages:
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@bluesky-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Mike Lowery <mike.lowery@bluesky-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer / marketplace MAP for Redwood evaluation & procurement

Hi Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send over a short summary of our expected buying path so we can confirm timelines: we're planning an initial 6-month evaluation with potential expansion to reserved capacity. We prefer a marketplace/private-offer flow if possible so our finance team can get clean billing and PO reconciliation.

Attached is the RFP excerpt for billing & procurement (Bluesky_RFP.pdf). Two quick questions to start:
- Do you typically support an AWS Private Offer (seller-created) and invoice via marketplace, or do you recommend a straight marketplace purchase?
- What's a realistic timeline from PO to signature for a $100k ARR start?

Would like to build a brief mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners so procurement can sign off. Can you loop in legal/finance as needed?

Thanks —
Sarah Jensen
Head of Procurement
BlueSky Analytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@bluesky-analytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer / marketplace MAP for Redwood evaluation & procurement

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the RFP. We can support both paths but there are trade-offs:
- AWS Private Offer (seller-created): cleaner commitment, can attach reserved capacity / Dedicated procurement, but requires us to provision the offer and your procurement to accept it — typically best when customers want committed spend.
- Marketplace purchase: faster for immediate trials, billing flows through Marketplace and is easier for customers who prefer standard AMI/invoice consolidation.

For a $100k ARR starter, realistic calendar: 2–3 weeks for MAP and PO confirmation (assuming legal review is light), 1–2 weeks for seller offer creation/acceptance if doing Private Offer, then provisioning + onboarding 1 week — target close in 4–6 weeks from MAP agreement.

I've drafted an initial MAP with milestones and owners attached (MAP-draft-connor-v1.docx). Proposed high-level milestones:
1) MAP sign-off (procurement + Redwood) — target Mar 27
2) Private Offer creation / Marketplace order path decision — target Apr 2
3) PO issuance from BlueSky — target Apr 6
4) Contract signature / DocuSign — target Apr 9
5) Provision & onboarding (dedicated capacity if requested) — target Apr 16

If your finance wants a sample invoice flow or a private-offer checklist, I can loop in our finance ops and legal. Shall we set a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk procurement through the MAP?

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@bluesky-analytics.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer / marketplace MAP for Redwood evaluation & procurement

Hi Sarah / Connor —

Quick legal/finance note from our side: if you go the AWS Private Offer route, our process is typically:
- Redwood creates the Private Offer in the AWS Marketplace with the agreed line items and effective dates.
- Customer (BlueSky) accepts the Private Offer in their AWS Marketplace console using the provided offer ID.
- Billing can then run via Marketplace (monthly invoices) or via direct invoicing if you have a corporate billing arrangement — we can support either but direct invoicing requires a short credit review.

What we need from you to start the Private Offer creation:
- AWS Marketplace Payer/Account ID (for acceptance)
- Finalized purchase line items (term, quantity)
- PO number and billing contact (if you prefer direct invoicing)

I attached a one-page cheatsheet on the Private Offer steps and typical lead times (PrivateOffer-cheatsheet.pdf). If you prefer marketplace billing, the time from offer to acceptance is often shorter since no PO is required and acceptance is self-serve.

Happy to join a call with your procurement team — I can cover contract redlines that typically show up (data retention, audit logs, SLA exceptions).

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Legal & Finance Partnerships
Redwood Inference

- Our finance prefers marketplace billing but will accept direct invoices if we can have standard NET30 terms and a PO.

Mike — looping you in. Can you confirm the AWS account id for acceptance? Also would like to confirm we can hit Mar 27 MAP sign-off if Redwood provides the MAP doc prior to EOD Thursday.

Sarah
